content.title: Today's weather: Snowstorm, tornado - here's what you need to track if you are staying in DC, Atlanta, Bos
content.text: Wild swings in weather are unfolding across several parts of the United States, leaving communities dealing with everything from tornado cleanup to snow threats and heavy rain. From the Midwest to the East Coast, the latest forecasts show a mix of severe storms, winter weather and rapidly changing temperatures.In Indiana, residents are beginning the difficult task of cleaning up after a deadly tornado outbreak earlier this week. Meanwhile, meteorologists are tracking multiple weather systems that could bring snow, rain and strong winds to regions including Washington D.C., Georgia and Massachusetts.Across these areas, officials are urging residents to stay alert as conditions evolve through the coming days. The information is sourced from various reports by ABC7 Chicago, CBS News, Fox5 DC, NBC Boston, WEAU13 News.How are Lake Village residents recovering after the deadly tornado?Residents of Lake Village, Indiana, woke up to another day of recovery after a powerful tornado tore through the community earlier in the week.Cleanup efforts are underway across the village as families and emergency crews work through the damage left behind by the storm.The tornado claimed the lives of Edward and Arlene Kozlowski, a husband and wife both in their 80s who had lived in their home for decades. Their deaths underscored the devastating toll the storm has taken on the small community.In the aftermath, many residents are still struggling to process what happened. "It's something you'll never forget for the rest of your life," Steve Travis said. "I can tell you that, right now."Thursday morning, nearly half of the village remained without electricity. Downed power lines continue to create hazards across the area, making power restoration one of the biggest priorities.Local officials have organized volunteer efforts to help clear debris. Volunteers were asked to gather starting at 8 a.m. to assist with cleanup across the community.At the same time, the Newton County Sheriff's Office is urging homeowners whose houses were destroyed to contact their insurance companies before beginning cleanup work on their own properties.The destruction has also brought neighbors together as the town begins to recover."It's nice living in a small community because a lot of people care," Michael Cox said. "You don't see that everywhere."Support services are also being offered locally. Donations are being collected at the community center, which has been providing meals for residents affected by the tornado.The center has also set up free Starlink internet service so people without connectivity can communicate with family and friends during recovery.What weather threats remain in Georgia today?While Indiana deals with the aftermath of tornado damage, strong storms are continuing across parts of Georgia.Early Thursday, the National Weather Service confirmed that a Tornado Watch remained in effect until 9 a.m. for areas of central and east-central Georgia.Earlier in the morning, the watch covered a larger portion of the state, but it was later cancelled for 19 counties in north-central and west-central Georgia as storms moved out.Areas where the watch was lifted include Clayton, Fayette, Henry and Rockdale counties in the Atlanta metro area, along with Coweta, Harris, Muscogee, Troup and Spalding counties.Cities such as Columbus, Peachtree City, Griffin and Newnan are no longer under the watch.However, several areas remain at risk. Counties including Bibb, Houston, Baldwin, Jones, Monroe, Peach, Pulaski, Putnam and Twiggs are still under the tornado watch, along with communities such as Macon, Warner Robins, Milledgeville, Cordele, Forsyth and Hawkinsville.The watch has also been expanded eastward to include counties such as Dodge, Laurens, Emanuel, Washington, Wilkes and Jefferson. Cities including Dublin, Vidalia, Sandersville and Swainsboro are now included in the watch area.Meteorologists say a line of strong to severe thunderstorms continues moving east across Georgia.Storms are traveling at about 35 miles per hour and could produce damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph, along with small hail and isolated tornadoes.Earlier Thursday morning, a tornado warning had been issued for parts of Marion, Chattahoochee and Webster counties before expiring shortly before 6 a.m. as the immediate threat weakened.Even where the tornado threat decreases, forecasters say the storms may still bring heavy rain, lightning and strong winds capable of damaging trees, roofs and siding.Local meteorologists also warn that localized flooding could develop during the morning commute where heavier rainfall occurs.Several school districts in Georgia delayed classes because of the weather threat.Meriwether County School System, Troup County School System and Rockdale County Public Schools all announced two-hour delays Thursday morning, citing severe weather concerns.Could Washington D.C. really see snow after record warmth?Weather conditions in Washington D.C. have taken an unusual turn this week.Temperatures surged into the middle 80s on both Tuesday and Wednesday, an exceptionally warm stretch for early spring.Wednesday’s high of 86°F marked the earliest point in the year that Washington D.C. has ever reached 86 degrees or higher.But that warmth may be short-lived. Forecasters say a fast-moving weather system could bring rain across the region Thursday, with the possibility that precipitation briefly changes to sleet or wet snow later in the day.Showers are expected to develop overnight and continue into the morning as a strong cold front moves through the Mid-Atlantic.Rain will likely dominate early in the day, with temperatures in the 50s around sunrise.As colder air pushes into the region, temperatures are expected to drop into the 40s and even the 30s during the afternoon.That cooling may allow rain to transition into sleet or snow late in the morning or early afternoon, first in western suburbs before moving eastward.Meteorologists say the changeover would likely depend on heavier precipitation rates cooling the atmosphere enough to allow snowflakes to form.Despite the unusual setup, significant snow accumulation is not expected.Ground temperatures remain warm, and any snow that falls would likely melt quickly once precipitation ends.Forecasters say disruptions are unlikely, though some areas that see heavier bursts of precipitation could briefly see snow collect on grassy surfaces.What conditions are expected in Massachusetts and the Upper Midwest?Another weather system is also being monitored across Massachusetts and surrounding areas.Rain fell heavily in some locations overnight, marking the wettest conditions expected over the next several days.Temperatures will gradually fall through the day as a cooler air mass settles into the region.Early highs in the 50s are expected to drop into the 40s by afternoon and into the 30s during the evening.Forecasters say a few snowflakes could appear later in the evening as the weather system exits.Friday should bring calmer conditions with highs in the mid to upper 40s.However, clouds will increase overnight and there could be snow showers over higher terrain in central Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire.The colder air is expected to persist through the weekend.Meanwhile, meteorologists are also tracking a larger storm expected to move through the region on Monday.That system is expected to be a warm storm bringing significant rainfall.Across the United States, communities are experiencing a wide range of weather conditions at once.From tornado recovery in Indiana to severe storms in Georgia and the unusual possibility of snow in Washington D.C., the coming days will keep meteorologists and residents closely watching the skies.As forecasts continue to evolve, officials are encouraging people to stay informed and prepared for rapidly changing conditions.FAQsWhich areas are facing major weather threats right now?Communities in Indiana, Washington D.C., Georgia and Massachusetts are dealing with severe weather impacts or forecasts.What types of weather are expected?The conditions include tornado recovery, strong thunderstorms, heavy rain and the possibility of snow in some areas.
